title: Decision in Paris to Ban E-scooters on Footpaths
what_it_is: Decision in Paris to Ban E-scooters on Footpaths

sections.label: E-scooter footpath rules abroad
sections.summary: Paris will ban e-scooters on footpaths, Berlin allows them at 12 km/h, and Queensland allows them at 25 km/h.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: For example, Paris will ban the use of e-scooters on footpaths, while Berlin will allow them but limits them to a device speed limit of 12 kilometres per hour (km/h).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Queensland in Australia allows e-scooters on footpaths but sets a higher device speed limit of 25 km/h.

sections.label: Singapore e-scooter footpath rules
sections.summary: A 2015 panel recommended allowing e-scooters on footpaths with rules, and over 1,630 offenders were caught under a registration regime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: In 2015, after an extensive public consultation, the Active Mobility Advisory Panel recommended that e-scooters be allowed on footpaths, but with a clear set of rules and code of conduct to ensure their safe use.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: We are mindful of the safety concerns expressed by Members as well as the general public.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: However, the solution is not to ban them, but to cultivate the right culture where users ride safely and responsibly and only at the allowed places.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: To date, more than 1,630 individuals have been caught for e-scooter-related offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: We have also introduced a mandatory e-scooter registration regime to facilitate identification of errant riders.

sections.label: LTA footpath device speed limit
sections.summary: LTA has reduced the speed limit of devices on footpaths from 15 km/h to 10 km/h.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: On the part of LTA, in order for us to make the footpaths safer for both pedestrians as well as PMD users, she may be aware that we have already reduced the speed limit of the devices on footpaths from 15 km/h to 10 km/h.

sections.label: Advice on sharing common spaces
sections.summary: Pedestrians and PMD users should exercise graciousness, caution and responsibility when sharing footpaths and shared paths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: As to the kind of advice that we give to pedestrians, whether it is the elderly or the young, as well as to the PMD users, I think we just have to exercise graciousness, caution as well as to act responsibly when we share the use of common spaces, such as footpaths and in shared paths.
